key_insight: Direct structural evidence does not yet prove that photoexcited carriers in lead-halide perovskites form polarons, and polaron formation should not be conflated with defect tolerance.
engineering_relevance: Accurate device design for perovskite solar cells depends on distinguishing carrier-lattice coupling from true defect-screening mechanisms, especially across realistic sunlight-level carrier densities.
method: Compare time-resolved lattice distortion measurements with theory across excitation densities.
Contrast carrier-lattice coupling mechanisms in 3D vs 2D perovskites (Ruddlesden-Popper and Dion-Jacobson).
Test defect tolerance separately from polaron screening using transport and structural probes.
evidence_signal: The abstract cites recent structural measurements, effective-mass calculations, and new transport data, but notes that these results do not directly establish polaron screening of defects.
watch_item: Ultrafast experiments often use much higher carrier densities than operating solar cells, so conclusions may not transfer to real device conditions.
paper_title: Polarons in Lead-Halide Perovskites: What the Structural Evidence Does and Does Not Establish
